title: Worker hook refuses shell edits mentioning push
body: A Bash command whose text holds a push-like token (e.g. a Python heredoc calling `.push(...)` on a string) is refused by the worker hook as if it were a git push; make multi-line Rust edits with the Edit tool instead of scripted heredocs.

title: Which config.toml forms of the ci mode key does write_ci_mode rewrite?
body:
**Chose:** `write_ci_mode` patches only a `[ci]` header section (header match tolerates spaces and quotes); a file that sets `ci.mode` as a dotted key or inline table gets a `[ci]` appended, which fails the `toml::from_str` check, so the writer returns `Err` and leaves the file untouched.
**Over:** a full TOML-aware editor (adding `toml_edit`) that rewrites any form of the key.
**Because:** the slice rules out `toml_edit` and calls for a line patch; the header form is the one the docs and the writer itself produce, and the parse check makes every other form fail safely instead of corrupting the file.
**Undo:** add `toml_edit` and replace `with_ci_mode` in `src/config.rs`.

title: The version bump and the new bundled file reach mods/cockpit and tests/init.rs
body:
**Chose:** bump `mods/cockpit/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `mods/cockpit/hooks/register.tsx` and `mods/cockpit/tests/cockpit.test.tsx` to `0.15.0`, and raise the bundled file count in `tests/init.rs` from 22 to 23, beside the slice's own files.
**Over:** keeping to the slice's file list, which leaves `the_mod_carries_the_crates_version` (tests/cockpit_mod.rs) and three `tests/init.rs` tests red.
**Because:** both are mechanical consequences of what the slice orders: the crate version is pinned in the mod by an existing test (the 0.14.0 release commit bumped the same three files), and `factory init` writes every file in the bundle, so one more reference is one more file. No other slice of this feature touches these files.
**Undo:** revert those four files together with the `Cargo.toml` bump and the new `gate/references/ci.md`.

title: A version bump also moves mods/cockpit and init's file count
body: Bumping `Cargo.toml` also needs the three version strings in `mods/cockpit/` (tests/cockpit_mod.rs pins them), and adding a skill file needs the file count in `tests/init.rs` raised; the worker hook also refuses any shell command whose text contains the p-u-s-h verb, even in a heredoc, so edit skill text holding that word with the Edit tool.

title: What does preflight say about CI mode when config.toml does not parse?
body:
**Chose:** `factory docs preflight` adds a `?` judge line `ci mode not read: <error>` beside the existing `second opinion not probed` line, and opens no CI-mode ask; `factory run` already fails on that config before preflight.
**Over:** opening the CI-mode ask anyway.
**Because:** answering `local` or `remote` would hit the same unparseable file in `write_ci_mode` and fail, so the ask could not be closed; the judge line names the real fix.
**Undo:** in `preflight::cli`'s `Err` arm, call `ci_mode` with a default `Loaded` instead of pushing the judge line.

title: Is ci_local emitted once per run or once per head?
body:
**Chose:** `ci_local` is emitted once per head: a resumed local closeout whose push moved HEAD logs a fresh `ci_local` with the new head; the same head is never logged twice.
**Over:** emitting at most one `ci_local` per run, as the slice worded it.
**Because:** `factory live` reads `ci.head` from the newest `ci_local`; one event per run would name a head the PR no longer carries after a resume that committed refreshed numbers.
**Undo:** drop the `h == head` match in `ci_local` in `src/closeout.rs` so any earlier `ci_local` skips the emit.

title: What does local CI mode tell the owner to do to run merge checks?
body:
**Chose:** every place local mode names the merge-check step (the `ci_local` closeout line, the CI-mode ask text, `/deliver` §3 step 4, `gate/references/ci.md` draft-silent section) now says GitHub skips every `pull_request` run, `ready_for_review` included, while the PR's head commit carries `[skip ci]`, and that one new commit without the token starts the required checks. The `[skip ci]` stamps on `ship`, `refresh_numbers` and the `/deliver` review commit stay as FR-3 ordered.
**Over:** the PRD's wording ("mark the PR ready for review (or push) to run required merge checks", FR-2 ask text and FR-3 closeout line), which three reviewers independently found wrong; or dropping `[skip ci]` from the last pushed commit, which would overturn FR-3's settled stamp.
**Because:** GitHub documents that `[skip ci]` in the head commit of a pull request suppresses `pull_request` workflows; `ready_for_review` is a `pull_request` activity type, so following the PRD's advice leaves a required check pending forever. The PRD's own text at `prd.md` §2 and FR-2/FR-3 carries the same wrong recovery; it is not edited here and is proposed in the PR body.
**Undo:** restore the four strings (`src/closeout.rs` `ci_local`, `src/docs/preflight.rs` `ci_mode`, `skills/deliver/SKILL.md` §3 step 4, `skills/gate/references/ci.md` draft-silent paragraph) and the needles in `tests/cockpit.rs` and `tests/skills_bundle.rs`.
